types.name: CuiSharp.ChartNormalizer
types.summary: Rescales a series against its baseline so several series share a comparable y range. The baseline is the first finite nonzero sample. A negative baseline is allowed and inverts the scale (-200 against -100 is Index100 200, not 50). The math is done in double and rounded to float once, so scaling does not compound rounding. A requested normalization rejects samples it cannot scale: NaN or infinity anywhere in the series, a series with no finite nonzero baseline (all zero, say), and results beyond the finite float range all throw ArgumentException rather than draw a line that silently lies. NaN is not a gap marker; the renderer has no gap concept. Copy-based and allocation-free like SeriesDecimator: the source is never mutated, results go into a caller-owned destination, and reuse keeps a frame at 0 B. The empty series is not an error — it means "nothing to draw" and returns 0. None keeps the old pass-through behavior, validation included, so opting out opts out of everything.

types.name: CuiSharp.Hosting.Mutation`1
types.summary: One background operation owned by a component: start it, keep drawing, and see the result on a later frame. The frame loop is synchronous, so nothing inside Draw may await. A mutation is the shape that makes that safe: it runs the work on the pool, holds the outcome, and never touches a Ui from a pool thread. While the operation runs — and for the one frame its result still needs to be drawn — the host keeps requesting frames, so the state appears immediately instead of on the next mouse move. Error and IsRunning are always current and cost nothing to read, so a fire-and-forget mutation needs no bookkeeping in Draw. Pass an apply callback when the result has to change state, and Draw never polls: the callback runs on the UI thread, before the next frame draws.

types.name: CuiSharp.Localization
types.summary: The month, weekday and "Today" names the date components show, for another language: the table SetLocalization hands to CUI. CUI keeps the pointer it is given and reads it every frame, so this table cannot live in the frame arena. This class owns one unmanaged block, rebuilt only when a name changes, and the surface that published it keeps this object alive and frees a replaced block at a frame boundary. Every entry is optional: a null falls back to the English name, so a partial table is a complete one. Weeks start on Monday, as in every CUI calendar, so Weekdays starts at Monday. A table belongs to one surface: publishing it to a second one throws, because only the surface that owns it is told when a name changes and a block is replaced.

types.name: CuiSharp.SeriesDecimator
types.summary: Reduces a long series to something a chart can draw in real time. A chart is a few hundred pixels wide, so points beyond roughly two per pixel cannot be seen — but they still cost geometry. members.name: AddFontFallback
members.summary: Adds a fallback CUI reaches for when font has no glyph. The chain holds at most four fallbacks; when it is exhausted CUI scans every other loaded face before giving up. A glyph no face has draws nothing at all — not even a .notdef box in every font — so an untranslated screen comes up blank with no warning. UseSystemFontFallback is the check for that, and the bundled faces are Latin. The glyph atlas is what a large script actually costs: one texture of CUI_ATLAS_MAX (4096) pixels per side, with the frame's glyph cache reset between frames, so a font that makes every frame load new glyphs is the expensive case. Register the faces a language needs at startup, not per frame.
